reads.macro_connection: June is where H.8 tracking begins. Small-bank funding was at its strongest — core deposits accreting, borrowings declining, cash at multi-month highs. Your credit union's 4% APY was the consumer expression of that competition for deposits. CPI at 3.3% and rising was starting to compress your real yield.
reads.monthly_note:
June was the household's deepest deficit month. Two mortgage payments landing in one statement period ($2,406) accounts for half the excess — one was the standard June payment, the other a pre-payment at month-end for July. Belle Tire ($560) was the other major one-off.

Investment transfers accelerated to $1,270, the highest of any month — $1,020 to RH Brokerage and $250 to Schwab. The household was simultaneously investing aggressively and running its thinnest liquidity cushion ($1,143). That's a high-conviction posture, but it left zero margin for unexpected expenses.

June is also where the H.8 tracking begins. Small-bank funding was at its peak — the strongest read in the dataset. Your credit union was part of that story, competing for deposits with a 4% checking rate. But with CPI climbing to 3.3%, the real yield on your deposits was quietly compressing from March's +1.2% to +0.7%.
